parsed_output.analysis: The model captures the overall structure (HumanDriving simple state, Autonomous submachine state, transitions on power on/off) reasonably well, but there are several deviations from the specification.

issues.issue: The transition condition 'in (AutoFinal)' is combined via OR with human_steering_cmd and brake_pressed on a single transition arrow from the Autonomous composite state, rather than being modeled as an automatic transition out of the AutoFinal substate.
issues.reason: The specification lists 'in (auto final)' as one of three distinct conditions that cause a transition back to human driving mode, alongside receiving a human steering command or brake pressed. Modeling it as an OR-ed guard condition on a transition from the composite state is a plausible but debatable interpretation; a more faithful representation would show a completion/automatic transition from the AutoFinal substate itself to HumanDriving, since reaching AutoFinal should unconditionally transition out (it's a terminal condition of the sub-machine, not a guard to be logically ORed with other event-driven triggers). As modeled, the semantics of 'in (AutoFinal)' as a guard evaluated on some triggering event is ambiguous, since guards without a specifying event won't fire automatically when AutoFinal is entered.

issues.issue: No explicit final state is shown inside the Autonomous submachine after AutoFinal, and there is no automatic transition from AutoFinal state to the enclosing final marker.
issues.reason: The spec implies the autonomous sub-machine reaches a final condition ('auto final') that should trigger a transition to human driving mode. The model's AutoFinal state has no exit transition to a submachine final node, so the 'in (AutoFinal)' condition on the outer transition is not clearly tied to an actual final-state completion event in the submachine, weakening the mapping to the spec's item 4 (transit to human driving when in auto final).
issues.where: Autonomous submachine (AutoInitial --> AutoFinal : Auto Process Complete; AutoFinal has no outgoing transition to [*])

issues.issue: The overall final state ('[*]' after Power Off) is only reachable from HumanDriving, but the specification states power off causes transition to final state without restricting from which state this can happen.
issues.reason: The specification's item 5 ('when power off, it will transit to final state') does not explicitly limit the power-off transition to only being valid while in HumanDriving mode; the model omits an equivalent Power Off transition from the Autonomous state, meaning the system cannot power off while autonomous, which may not conform to the intended global behavior.

issues.issue: The entry and internal transition labels in the Autonomous submachine ('Enter Autonomous Mode', 'Auto Process Complete') are not defined or mentioned anywhere in the specification.
issues.reason: These are invented events/triggers not present in the specification, which only mentions front_distance, human_steering_cmd, brake_pressed, power on/off, and reaching auto final; introducing undocumented triggers goes beyond what was specified and may not reflect actual system behavior.
issues.where: state Autonomous { [*] --> AutoInitial : Enter Autonomous Mode; AutoInitial --> AutoFinal : Auto Process Complete }

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1 The human driving mode is represented by a simple state. 2 The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state. 3. when power on, the system turn into human driving mode 4when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state 4. transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final) 5 when power off, it will transit to final state

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
[*] --> HumanDriving : Power On
HumanDriving : Human Driving Mode

HumanDriving --> Autonomous : front_distance > 10
state Autonomous {
[*] --> AutoInitial : Enter Autonomous Mode
AutoInitial --> AutoFinal : Auto Process Complete
AutoFinal : Auto Final State
}

Autonomous --> HumanDriving : human_steering_cmd || brake_pressed || in (AutoFinal)
HumanDriving --> [*] : Power Off
@enduml
